    Hi everyone,

    We successfully managed to make Windows on ARM and Ubuntu 26.04 work on Android devices using the Qualcomm Gunyah hypervisor.

    This is done with a bunch of ported pieces, including drivers, EDK2 firmware work, and other VM-related components needed to make the guest OS boot and run properly on the phone.

    This is not traditional emulation like qemu-tcg/Bochs. The idea is to use the phone’s native virtualization support, so the guest system can run much closer to native speed.

    Current status:
    • Windows on ARM boots and runs
    • Ubuntu 26.04 also works as a guest
    • Basic display/input are working
    • Some drivers have been ported
    • EDK2/firmware pieces are working enough to boot the VM
    • Mainly tested on newer Snapdragon devices with Gunyah support
    For 3D acceleration, we currently have a few ideas. One possible direction is something like DXVK inside the Windows kernel, then forwarding Vulkan calls through gfxstream to host. The problem is that the first part basically does not exist yet, and the second part is not working for us right now. So 3D acceleration is still very much a work in progress, but we are actively trying different approaches.

    It is still very experimental, so don’t expect a daily-driver experience yet. There are still many things missing or unstable, especially around graphics acceleration, device compatibility, and drivers.

    Demo / screenshots:


    Source code:

    GitHub - Droid-VM/DroidVM: Run virtual machine on Android Phones

    Run virtual machine on Android Phones. Contribute to Droid-VM/DroidVM development by creating an account on GitHub.
    github.com

    I’m posting this here to see if anyone is interested in testing, hacking on it, or helping with the lower-level parts. Help would be especially useful around:
    • Gunyah / protected VM support
    • Windows ARM drivers
    • virtio-gpu / gfxstream / 3D acceleration
    • EDK2 / firmware
    • Snapdragon device compatibility
    The long-term goal is to make Android phones able to run desktop ARM operating systems with native virtualization instead of slow emulation.

    Thanks!

    We succesfully managed to make the minecraft 26.2 and wine+dxvk works on Ubuntu 26.04 VM on my android device(Lenovo Y700 Gen4), based on Virtio-GPU + Gfxstream.

    Requirements:
    1. Gunyah available device(snapdradon 8 gen 3 and newer chip)
    2. Root permission
    3. kernel module loadable (knox and some vender security mechanism prevents kmod loading)
    The performance is roughtly 50% compare to host, measured by vkmark.

    We are working on three parts now:
    1. kgsl native context for virtio-gpu(forward ioctls to host, make /dev/kgsl-3d0 available in guest). if this work, we can get 99% GPU performance
    2. GPU driver for windows, make 3D acceleration available on windows guest
    3. improve the performance and stability for gfxstream, make it more useable
    Welcome to join us if you get interested on this
